facts: Karnataka Handloom Development Corporation Limited is a Public Sector Enterprise established by the Karnataka State Government.
The respondent was appointed for various spells of fixed periods on a fixed honorarium as an expert weaver to train the weavers in the unorganized sector.
The State Government introduced 'VISHWA' programme to train and rehabilitate the weavers.
The Labour Department referred the dispute u/s. 10(1)(c) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 for adjudication.

The appellant-Corporation is a Public Sector Enterprise established by the Karnataka State Government to promote and assist the growth and development of the Handloom Industry outside the Cooperative sector in the State.
The respondent was appointed specifically under the scheme on contract basis in February, 1993 for a period of 3 months on different terms of pay of Rs.1,000/- per month.
He was again appointed on contract basis for a period of 9 months as per the terms set out in the letter of appointment.
After the expiry of the contract of appointment, on 31.08.1994, he was not appointed again.
The Labour Court allowed the reference, in part, directing reinstatement without back wages.
Aggrieved by the award, the Corporation preferred a writ petition, which was dismissed by a Single Judge.
The writ appeal filed by the appellant-Corporation was also dismissed by the Division Bench of the High Court.
issues: Whether the I.D. Act applies to the respondent
Whether the respondent is a workman in the employment of the appellant-Corporation
petitioner_arguments: The respondent was not a workman in the employment of the appellant-Corporation

The respondent was engaged on contract basis for fixed periods only and later under a specific scheme/Vishwa programme introduced by the State and that the scheme has already been closed and as such there are no funds for continuing with the said scheme.
There is no relationship of employee and employer between the Corporation and the weavers
The master weavers who are engaged by the Corporation to give training to the weavers in the matter of weaving of cloth cannot be considered as a workman
respondent_arguments: The respondent had worked with the appellant-Corporation from 1987 to 1994 i.e. more than 240 days as contemplated under Section 25B of the I.D. Act
His dismissal amounted to retrenchment within the meaning of S. 2(oo) of the I.D. Act
court_reasoning: The nature of work entrusted to the respondent is to carry out the usual business of selling the cotton yarn or polyster to weavers who are covered under the scheme of the Corporation.

The said weavers who purchased the yarn, after converting into a finished product in the form of cloth, sell the same to the respondent, the sale value of the finished product is credited to the account of each such weaver.

These weavers are also provided loans by the banks, KFFC and such banking or financial institutions and the same is kept as a security with the respondent towards raw material provided to the weavers and also looms and accessories.
holding: The court held that the respondent's appointment was purely contractual and for a specified period.
He is not eligible to any other benefits as a regular employee of the Corporation and could be liable for termination without any notice and without payment of compensation.
The case of the claimant, therefore, in our view, does not become an industrial dispute.
